cards.explanation: The answer is Capernaum. John 6:24 says the crowd got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him. A whole crowd climbing into boats just to track Him down. Friends, I've seen less hustle at a free cookie sample tray.
The answer is that they ate the loaves and had their fill. Jesus tells them, "…you ate the loaves and had your fill." He doesn't even answer the when question. He goes straight to the why.

The word is eternal. Jesus says to work for "…food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you." A cookie on my counter lasts maybe a week if I hide it from myself. Jesus is talking about food that endures to eternal life.

The answer is to believe in the One He has sent. Jesus says, "The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent." The crowd asked about works, plural, and He gives them one. I think that's a lot simpler than I'd have guessed.

The answer is manna. The crowd says, "Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness…" They bring it up right after asking, "What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You?" (John 6:30). I think they're hoping Jesus will top that menu.

The answer is False. Moses, Israel's leader, is not the giver here. Jesus says, "…it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven." The giver is the Father, and the bread He gives is the true bread from heaven.

The word is hunger. Jesus says, "Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst." He says it right after "I am the bread of life." Friends, I've never made a cookie that did that, and I've made a LOT of cookies.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away." If you come, He doesn't send you off. I've been in a place where I thought nobody wanted me, so I know how good that sounds.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me." He came to do the will of the One who sent Him. The next verse tells what that will is.

The answer is that He will raise them up. Jesus says the will of the One who sent Him is that He "…shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day." He loses none of them. My ovens stay warm, friends, because that's something to get ready for.

The answer is that they know His father and mother. The grumblers say, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?" They bring up His father and mother as part of their question. I think that's a hard thing to hear about someone whose family you know.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day." He says it right after telling them to stop grumbling. The Father is the one doing the drawing.

The answer is True. Jesus says no one has seen the Father "…except the One who is from God; only He has seen the Father." That is a big claim about Himself. And it comes right after He quotes the Prophets about being taught by God.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died." He says it right after calling Himself the bread of life. That sets up the bread that doesn't end in death.
The word is die. Jesus says, "This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die." Notice the word anyone, friends. That means no special club.
The answer is His flesh. Jesus says, "And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh." He gives it for the life of the world. That's a big thing to say in a synagogue.

The answer is that they have no life in them. Jesus says, "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you." The Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). He opens with "Truly, truly," like He did earlier in this passage.

The answer is that whoever eats His flesh and drinks His blood remains in Jesus and Jesus in him. Jesus says, "Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him." Jesus in him and him in Jesus. That's a close bond, friends.

The word is synagogue. John 6:59 says, "Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum." So that's where He was teaching when He said all this. I like to picture the people in the back leaning in.
